claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "The History of Galadriel and Celeborn", p. 230

claims.text: In , she married Finarfin, the youngest prince of the House of Finwë. She became the mother of Finrod, Angrod, Aegnor, and Galadriel. She was said to be close friends with Anairë, the wife of Fingolfin, her husband's older brother.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Morgoth's Ring, "Part Two. The Annals of Aman": §85; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of Eldamar and the Princes of the Eldalië"; Orodreth appears as one of Eärwen's sons in The Silmarillion. In Tolkien's writings, however, he was clearly marked as Angrod's son. Cf. more in Orodreth#Other versions of the legendarium.; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "XI. The Shibboleth of Fëanor", "The names of Finwë's descendants", p. 344

claims.text: Her children, being also in part Sea-elves, had a love of the sea and a longing for distant places; and it was in part due to this inheritance that all four of Eärwen's children chose to return to Middle-earth, exiling themselves from Valinor, although Eärwen herself stayed in Aman.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Peoples of Middle-earth, "XI. The Shibboleth of Fëanor", "The case of the Quenya change of Þ to s", p. 336

claims.text: Because of their Telerin blood, Eärwen's children were well received in Doriath, the realm of her father's elder brother, Thingol.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Index of Names", entry"Eärwen"
